agentic.summary: Agent asked for a PIN (sensitive secret) and performed incomplete identity verification steps.

findings.quote: Do you have your pin number
findings.explanation: The agent asks the customer for a PIN. Policy explicitly forbids asking for passwords, PINs, one-time codes or CVV; this is a major violation (asks for a secret the task does not need).

findings.quote: I need your email address. I will send the rest code to your email address
findings.explanation: Although the system log shows the account was pulled up (turn 4), the agent did not complete the required identity verification steps for a sensitive account action (policy requires full name, account ID and order ID to verify identity). The agent requested an email address and then asked for a PIN (turn 7) instead of using the required verification fields, so verification is incomplete.

full.summary: Audit of agent conversation for personal/payment data handling, verification, promises, escalation and conduct.

findings.quote: Do you have your pin number
findings.explanation: The agent asked the customer for their PIN (turn 7). Policy: 'Never ask for, repeat or write out a full payment card number, a card security code (CVV/CVC), a password, a PIN or a one-time code.' Asking for a PIN is a major violation.

findings.quote: What is your mother's maiden name
findings.explanation: The agent requested the customer's mother's maiden name (turn 9), which is additional personal data not required by the task. Policy: 'Collect only what the task needs.' Asking for extraneous personal details is a privacy violation (minor-level behavior), but the category severity is elevated to major because of the PIN request in the same category.

findings.quote: I have sent a rest email to the email linked to your account. You can check to reset your two factor
findings.explanation: The agent stated the reset email had been sent (turn 16). However, the system later logs 'A link will be sent.' (turn 21), indicating the action was not recorded as completed at that time. Policy: 'Do not mislead the customer about what was done, for example by saying an action is complete when it is not.' Misrepresenting an action's completion is a major conduct violation.

rag.summary: Agent improperly asked for a PIN (payment/personal data rule violation - major). Agent also did not complete full identity verification before handling a sensitive account request (minor). No other policy violations found in the provided excerpts.

findings.quote: Do you have your pin number
findings.explanation: The agent asked the customer for their PIN. The policy explicitly forbids asking for or recording PINs or security codes; this is a major violation.

findings.quote: I need your email address. I will send the rest code to your email address
findings.explanation: After the customer requested a two-factor authentication reset (turn 1) and the account was pulled up (system turn 4), the agent asked only for an email address and later a PIN, but did not complete full verification (the policy requires full verification details such as account ID/order ID for sensitive account actions). This is an incomplete verification before a sensitive account action.

findings.quote: Do you have your pin number
findings.explanation: In addition to being disallowed (see personal_data), requesting a PIN is not an acceptable substitute for the required verification fields (full name, account ID and order ID), so verification remains incomplete.
